newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to call up army reserves for rebel fight.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to call up army reserves for rebel fight.

text.p: The government plans to call up military reserves to contain a growing threat posed by leftist guerrillas, Colombia's Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra said in an interview with a newspaper published on Tuesday.

"Some military reserve members will be called on during the first few days of October," he told El Tiempo, Colombia's leading newspaper. "We still don't know how many or under what conditions but they are going to be called into service."

Esguerra conceded that Colombia has been hard hit by a surge in rebel attacks since late last month in which at least 200 people have been killed and more than 60 soldiers were taken prisoner. But he said many of the rebel attacks appeared to have been carried out for publicity purposes more than anything else and "making people believe that they (the guerrillas) are more numerous than they really are."

The National Liberation Army (ELN), the second-largest rebel group, has dynamited Colombia's main oil pipeline, erected roadblocks across major highways and torched at least 50 vehicles since it launched a nationwide offensive against the government of President Ernesto Samper on Friday.
At dawn on Tuesday, ELN guerrillas set 10 buses and three private vehicles on fire in a parking lot on the outskirts of Cali, Colombia's second largest city.

Army chief Gen. Harold Bedoya has complained in recent interviews that Colombia's military was too small to mount an effective counterinsurgency campaign. "We have 100,000 soldiers for a country that should have at least 360,000," he said.
